info.title: VRChat Feedback Search (SearchKit gateway)
info.description: Nginx exposes this API at the public search host. `POST /api/search` accepts the Algolia multi-query JSON array used by `@searchkit/instantsearch-client`. `GET /api/search` implements **only** the single-query subset described under that path: same index (`feedback-posts`), same `params.query` / `hitsPerPage` / `page` mapping to SearchKit, and the same Algolia-shaped **search** response as an equivalent one-element POST. **GET adds non-search discovery responses** (no POST equivalent — see GET operation / *Contract gaps & GET-only botches*). Full contract notes live in this file only (served at `/openapi.json`).

tags.name: Search
tags.description: `/api/search` — POST is the full InstantSearch client payload; GET is a thin query-string projection of **one** query worth of `params` plus GET-only discovery.

post.description: Passes the request body verbatim to SearchKit `handleRequest`. This is the only method that supports multiple queries per request, replica / sort indices, facets, filters, and every other InstantSearch `params` field. **There is no POST discovery mode** (no body shape returns the small JSON stub that GET returns with no params). **400** if the body is not a JSON array.

schema.description: InstantSearch multiple-queries array. Minimum useful element for parity with GET “simple search” is a single object with `indexName`: `feedback-posts` and `params` containing at most `query`, `hitsPerPage`, and `page` (other keys are GET-inexpressible).

200.description: Algolia-compatible search results envelope (never the GET discovery stub).

400.description: Body was not a JSON array.

get.summary: Single-query search via query string (POST subset only) or discovery JSON
get.description:
## Search parity with POST

If **any** of `q`, `query`, `hitsPerPage`, or `page` is present, the handler builds exactly **one** `MultipleQueriesQuery`:

- `indexName`: `feedback-posts`
- `params.query`: from `q` if set, else `query` (**see botch:** both present → `query` ignored)
- `params.hitsPerPage`: parsed integer in **1…100**, default **15** if missing; invalid or **≤0** → **15** (**GET-only coercion** — POST leaves omitted keys to SearchKit defaults)
- `params.page`: non-negative integer, default **0** if missing; invalid or negative → **0**

That array is passed to the same `handleRequest` as POST. So for the **intersection** of features (plain text query + page size + page index on the primary index only), **GET and POST return the same search payload shape**.

## POST-only (not expressible on GET)

Extra `params` keys (facets, numeric filters, `sortBy` / replica index names, geo, etc.), a second query object, or a different `indexName` — **POST only**.

## Contract gaps & GET-only botches

1. **Discovery JSON** — With **no** `q`, `query`, `hitsPerPage`, or `page`, the response is a small JSON stub (`endpoints`, `description`) pointing at POST and `/openapi.json`. **POST has no equivalent.**
2. **Duplicate query keys** — If `q` or `query` is repeated (`?q=a&q=b`), Express may supply an array; **only the first value** is used.
3. **`q` vs `query`** — If both are set, **`q` wins**; `query` is ignored.
4. **`help` removed** — The gateway no longer treats `help` as a special query parameter. It is **ignored** for routing (same as any other unknown key). If **no** search parameters are present, the response is still the discovery stub — so `GET /api/search?help=1` alone behaves like a bare `GET /api/search`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Maps to `params.query`. Takes precedence over `query` when both are sent.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Synonym of `q`; ignored if `q` is also set.

parameters.name: hitsPerPage
parameters.description: Maps to `params.hitsPerPage`. Omitted → 15. Invalid or ≤0 → 15 (server coercion).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Maps to `params.page`. Omitted → 0. Invalid or negative → 0.

200.description: Either (a) Algolia-shaped **search** results — same envelope as POST for the parity case — or (b) the **discovery** stub JSON when none of `q`, `query`, `hitsPerPage`, or `page` is sent.

500.description: Search execution failed upstream (discovery mode does not use SearchKit).

options.summary: CORS preflight; often answered by nginx before the gateway.
options.description: The edge may return **204** via nginx (`OPTIONS` → 418 internal route). Behavior depends on deployment; not part of search parity.
